note: pub fns with no caller outside a test, each with the reason it is unreached. Checked by tools/check-production-callers.mjs. The ratchet only tightens: a name here that gains a production caller fails the check until it is removed, and a new unreached fn fails until it is either wired up or added with a reason. Every entry was triaged on 2026-09-16 and none now reads `not triaged`; the reasons below are the four kinds there turned out to be — a producer that does not exist yet, a seam a test supplies a fake through, surface whose only caller is outside this workspace, and a second spelling of a rule enforced elsewhere. Never add a name without an argument for it: a list of names with no reasons is the thing this list exists to prevent, and a reason that names a caller should be checked before it is believed — `check_code` and `tier_profile_to_json` each named one that did not exist. Checking both is what settled them: `check_code` was deleted, and `tier_profile_to_json` was kept for a reason its own comment had never given.

allowed.from_u64: §19 forbids a robot holding a signing key, so `skynet-ed25519` is verification-only and its description says so. The signer exists behind `#[cfg(feature = "test-signing")]` because a test proving the *verified* path needs a signature over bytes it chose, and the alternative is testing the verifier against four fixed messages forever. A dev-dependency cycle back to this package turns the feature on for its own tests without putting it in anything that ships.
allowed.from_seed: As `from_u64` — behind `test-signing`, which nothing that ships may name.
allowed.verifying_key: As `from_u64` — behind `test-signing`, which nothing that ships may name.
allowed.public_hex: As `from_u64` — behind `test-signing`, which nothing that ships may name.
allowed.sign_hex: As `from_u64` — behind `test-signing`, which nothing that ships may name.
allowed.estimated: §47.4's producer side. No capture backend exists on this edition — `skynet-capture` moves handles a V4L2 or GenICam backend would produce and neither is written — so the API a backend calls is unreached by construction rather than by oversight. Phase 1 of DRY-COVERAGE-PLAN.md is what reaches it.
allowed.is_full: As `estimated` — §47.4's producer side, waiting on a capture backend.
allowed.close_gap: As `estimated` — §47.4's producer side, waiting on a capture backend.
allowed.open_gap: As `estimated` — §47.4's producer side, waiting on a capture backend.
allowed.deliver: As `estimated` — §47.4's producer side, waiting on a capture backend.
allowed.revoke_loans: §47.6's frame pool. The loan and the mapping are built and three editions reproduce them; the pixels are not, so the pool a robot offers today is empty and nothing has a loan to revoke. Same unblocker as `estimated`.
allowed.from_environment: §25's producer end, and the same unblocker as `estimated`. `skynetd` sets the two rendezvous variables for the package it supervises as the policy; the policy runtime that would read them is the half of §25 that is not built, which `docs/status.md` states on its own behalf. A caller appears when there is a policy process to call it.
allowed.from_flags: The vendor ABI's Rust view (§4, §31.2). This crate is public surface for a driver author outside this workspace, so an in-workspace caller is not expected — and `skynetd-io` deliberately has no edge to it (§33.1), which is why §24's flag values are restated there and held by tools/check-rhal-flags.mjs instead.
allowed.write_response: Its doc gives the reason: exposed so a caller running its own loop writes the same bytes. §32.2's console and the local API both go through `serve`, which encodes responses itself, so the spelling exists to stop an embedder inventing a second encoder rather than to be called from here.
allowed.format_pairing_code: Confirmed 2026-09-16, which the previous entry asked for rather than assumed: the Hub is the caller. `lib/skynet/fleet.ts:194` in the Robot Overflow tree renders a pairing code through its mirrored copy at `lib/skynet/os/identity.ts:216`. §10 gives the robot the other half — it checks a code a person typed at it and never prints one — so the only caller is across the repository boundary, which is exactly where this contract is mirrored to.
allowed.with_links: Its doc says so: the seam the tests use. `Discovery` is built over real sockets in production and over links a caller supplies in the suite, which is how §82's responder is exercised without a network. Unreached is the design, not an oversight.
allowed.accepting: A recording `Enrolment` that accepts, returning the enrolled identity — the fake behind §10's pairing exchange, so a test can prove the enrolled path without an HTTPS request. Production constructs the real one.
allowed.with_units: A fake systemd, arranged with the state the machine will report. §33.1's launcher is exercised against it where CI has no manager; production builds the one that talks to the real one.
allowed.rooted: A `Power` reader rooted at a tree the caller supplies, which is how §36's gauge is exercised on a host with no battery — its own doc says as much. Production uses the sysfs paths §28 pins.
allowed.transfers: A second spelling of a set §75's fetch loop deliberately writes out. `skynetd-io/src/bundle.rs:591` matches `Fetch | Resume | DiscardAndFetch` exhaustively, and that is the better code: a boolean lets a new `FetchDecision` variant compile and pick a side in silence, where the match makes it an error at the one place that acts on the decision. Keeping it as the enum's named vocabulary or deleting it are both defensible; wiring it in is not.
allowed.read_path: The module's own reads go through the private `read`, which returns a `Value` and so keeps an absent member distinguishable from a `null` one — the distinction §54.2 exists for. `read_path` flattens that to `Option`, which is the right shape for a caller outside the crate and the wrong one for the evaluator. The Python edition spells its *internal* helper with this name, which is why the two look like one function and are not.
allowed.role_key_of: A convenience over `parse_role(role).map(|p| p.key())`. `skynet-contracts/src/lib.rs:90` re-exports `parse_role` and `ParsedRole` and not this, and no caller in the workspace asks the question in one step. Two lines, and nothing is waiting on them.
allowed.asks_for_us: Superseded by something finer. `Responder::heard` has to know *which* question matched — a shared record, a unique one, or one wanting a unicast answer — so it asks `asks_about_service` per question rather than once per message. This collapses the same decision to one bool over the whole message, which the responder cannot use.
allowed.power_refusal: Superseded, and deliberately. `power_refusal_from` takes a reading the caller already holds and sits on the reconcile pass at `skynetd-io/src/runtime.rs:1761`, so §36.1's withholding of new task leases *is* enforced. This one takes the gauge itself, which is the hazard its sibling's own doc names: two reads in one pass would let a skill be refused a lease for a battery level its precondition had just cleared. An unreached public function that does the thing the code beside it warns against is a trap for the next caller; removing it is the owner's call rather than this list's.
allowed.needs_side_count: An accessor on the URDF import report. The same count is taken at `skynet-urdf/src/descriptor.rs:268`, from the suggestions and before the report exists, so the inline spelling cannot call this one; and the CLI prints the notes rather than the counts. A second spelling whose halves cannot be folded in the obvious direction.
allowed.clean: `Report::clean` on the driver-admission report — whether anything at all was wrong. Its callers act on the findings themselves rather than on a summary, so the yes/no question has nobody to ask it. Kept as the report type's own vocabulary.
allowed.lock_path: An accessor on `Writership`. §26.2's writership is taken, held and dropped, and where the lock file sits is a fact the suite asserts about; production derives every path under §28 from the layout rather than reading one back off the lock.
allowed.grants_by_package: *For a report*, and no report groups grants by package. §54's grants are checked where they are used, and `skynet skills` prints what the launcher reports running. The shape somebody wants the day there is a grants page; unreached until there is one.
allowed.grants_for: `Actual::grants_for` — the tokens granted to one package. Nothing asks the per-package question; the reconciler works from the grant list as a whole. Same family as `grants_by_package`, one crate down.
allowed.bundle_message: The eighth signature tag. §56.2's run bundle binds a policy, an embodiment and an OS image digest, and this is the message a device's signature over one is made over. Its siblings are all reached — `package_message` at `runtime.rs:518`, `embodiment_message` at `embodiment.rs:316` — and this one is not, because nothing on a robot yet produces or verifies a run bundle. §19 forbids the robot holding a signing key, so the verifying side is the half that would appear first.
allowed.next_due_ms: Its doc names the caller it would save — one that would otherwise poll blindly — and `skynetd-io/src/discovery.rs:242` polls blindly, asking `due(now_ms)` every reconcile pass. Wiring it would make §82.4's responder a timer rather than a poll. Real and small, and left because the pass has a fixed period regardless: this is a scheduling change, not a correctness one.
allowed.tier_profile_to_json: Nearly deleted on 2026-09-16 for naming a surface that does not exist, and kept once the body was read: it is the **only place in the workspace that renders `SAFETY_CLAIM_RULE` into an output**. `skynet-kernel` declares the sentence and CI checks the text is intact; nothing else emits it. CONTRIBUTING.md requires every surface that mentions the certified tier to render it in full, so deleting the one renderer would have left that rule with nothing implementing it and no check able to notice. Built ahead of its surface, not unused — and the rule is carried on every tier rather than only the certified one so that a surface cannot render a tier without also holding the sentence that qualifies it.
allowed.notifies_operator: **A gap rather than a spelling, and the same shape as `Transition::warning`.** §36.1 derives three facts from a power state and the other two reach a surface: `power_to_json` serialises `requires_safe_state` and `stops_immediately` (`skynet-contracts/src/json.rs:1392`) and the CLI renders both. This one is in neither the document the daemon serves nor the daemon itself — nothing under `crates/skynetd-io/src` or `crates/skynetd/src` matches on `PowerState::Low`, `Reserve` or `Critical` at all — so the row that says an operator is told is computed, tested, and told to nobody. Closing it is a wire change: a field on the power document, the TypeScript oracle, the corpus's 28 power cases and four editions. Named here rather than done quietly. F7 in DRY-COVERAGE-PLAN.md.
allowed.driver_may_activate: Half-folded on 2026-09-16, and the half that is left is the structural one. The predicate — §19's rule that only a `verified` signature admits — now lives once, on `SignatureState::admits`, and both this and the daemon's activation arm (`skynetd-io/src/runtime.rs`) ask it, so a third spelling is a change to one function. What this still has that the contract cannot is the `NotRun` arm: admission that could not be assessed is not admission that passed. It stays unreached because `runtime.rs` never builds a `Report` — `main.rs` builds one to *print*, not to gate — and joining those two paths is a larger refactor than §78's remedy called for.
